title: A Hierarchical and Disentangling Interest Learning Framework for Unbiased and True News Recommendation

problem.claim: News recommender systems must help users discover relevant news efficiently, but existing systems face issues that reduce recommendation quality.

gap.claim: Existing systems often oversimplify hierarchical reading interests and disregard fake news and political bias in real-world contexts.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces the Hierarchical and Disentangling Interest learning framework (HDInt).
HDInt combines hierarchical interest learning with disentangling interest learning.
The framework models high- and low-level interests and separates polarity and veracity information from news content.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present HDInt as a novel framework addressing the identified gaps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on two real-world datasets.
The authors report that HDInt outperforms state-of-the-art news recommender systems for accurate, unbiased, and true recommendations.

narrative_sequence.summary: News recommender systems support efficient discovery of users' interests.
Existing systems have recommendation-quality issues caused by simplified interest modeling and unrealistic context assumptions.
The paper introduces HDInt with hierarchical and disentangling interest learning modules.
The modules model hierarchical interests and separate polarity from veracity to support fairness- and truth-aware recommendations.
Experiments on two real-world datasets are reported to show superiority over state-of-the-art systems.

source_observation.claim: User interests may span hierarchical levels from event-related interests to article-specific interests.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation models may benefit from representing interests at multiple levels of abstraction.

application.claim: Model both high-level topics or events and low-level item-specific preferences when designing news recommendation systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether hierarchical interest modeling is beneficial outside the reported news recommendation setting.

source_observation.claim: Fake news and political bias can affect recommendation outcomes in real-world contexts.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation objectives may need to account for content attributes beyond relevance and accuracy.

application.claim: Consider separating and modeling content polarity and veracity when developing fairness- and truth-aware recommenders.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how fairness or truthfulness is operationalized or measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two datasets.
The abstract does not provide evaluation metrics or numerical results.
The abstract does not specify the state-of-the-art baselines.
The abstract does not describe the implementation or training details of the modules.
